name: Jin Lianqin
current_role: Director and largest shareholder (~29.9%), Jiangsu Changqingshu New Materials Technology Co. (Changqing Technology, SSE: 603125)
profile: Jin Lianqin (金连琴), 59, is a director and co-controlling shareholder (with her husband, chairman Sun Qiuxin) of Zhenjiang-based Changqing Technology, a maker of specialty monomers and polymer additives that listed on the Shanghai main board in April 2023. She also heads Xinxin Oil Products and is GM of Zhenjiang Baoju Oil Additives.
interesting_fact: Changqing's predecessor was set up in June 2010 as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise held via a British nominee, Alan David Pow, on Sun Qiuxin's behalf to fit local investment-attraction policy; the nominee arrangement was unwound in Dec 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals, she spent 13 years (1990-2003) as a clinical lab staffer in the testing department of the Danmian Group staff hospital, then worked in the lab of Danyang Yunyang People's Hospital until 2006.
notes: Hurun 'Changqing' = Changqing Technology (常青科技, 603125), not Changqing Agrochemical (002391). Low public profile; best route is the company securities office (board secretary).

name: Su Zhuangqi
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Su Suyu, Su Wuxiong, Su Guanrong, Su Zhuangqiang) of Lianmei Quantum Co. (formerly Lianmei Holding, SSE: 600167); not listed as an executive
profile: Su Zhuangqi (苏壮奇) is a member of the Su family that controls Lianmei Group and its Shenyang-based listed arm Lianmei Quantum (formerly Lianmei Holding), a clean district-heating and integrated energy utility that also runs high-speed-rail digital media advertising. He is a named acting-in-concert party holding ~1.25% via the controlling structure; he appeared on Hurun China 2008-2015 with Su Suyu.
interesting_fact: Lianmei Quantum's core business is clean heating for Shenyang plus power and steam, and it also operates a high-speed-rail station digital advertising business - an unusual utility-plus-media combination.
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in filings or open web. Brother/relative Su Zhuangqiang is chairman. Alive status not explicitly confirmed, but he is still named as an acting-in-concert controller in the 2026 H1 report. Route: Lianmei Quantum securities dept.

name: May Makhzoumi
current_role: President, Makhzoumi Foundation (Lebanon); board member, Future Pipe Industries and other Future Group companies; Chairperson, Future Management Services Ltd (London)
profile: May Naamani Makhzoumi is a Lebanese-British philanthropist and businesswoman, wife of Future Pipe Industries founder Fouad Makhzoumi; the family fortune comes from FPI, a global maker of fibreglass pipe systems. She chairs London-based Future Management Services, sits on Future Group boards and has led the Makhzoumi Foundation (vocational training, micro-credit, healthcare) since 2000.
interesting_fact: The Makhzoumi Foundation, set up in 1997, says it has reached more than 650,000 people across Lebanon; she was the only Lebanese representative at UNESCO's 2014 World Conference on Education for Sustainable Development.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a pharmacist (BSc Pharmacy, AUB, 1975) and worked as an out-patient pharmacist in Beirut and then at King Faisal's Hospital in Riyadh (1975-77) before joining the family business in London.
notes: Email is from her expert profile on LAU's 'Who Is She in Lebanon' directory (profiles are typically self-submitted); a second, malformed variant is also listed there. Husband Fouad Makhzoumi is a Lebanese MP; keep outreach non-political.

name: Xu Limin
current_role: Vice Chairman and Director, Beijing Oriental Yuhong Waterproof Technology Co. (SZSE: 002271)
profile: Xu Limin (许利民), born 1966 and a Peking University graduate, is described in company filings as a principal co-founder of Oriental Yuhong, China's largest waterproofing-materials maker. He joined in 1998 and rose from vice GM to executive vice GM to vice chairman, a role he still holds; he owns roughly 72 million shares.
interesting_fact: Oriental Yuhong, founded in 1995 and listed in Shenzhen in 2008, has gone global: it set up a plant in Trinidad and Tobago with Lake Asphalt (2013) and broke ground on a factory and logistics centre in Prairie View, Texas in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond waterproofing, he has been executive director of a Beijing film and TV media company, Beijing Xingle Yinghua Film & Television Culture Media, since 2011, and was a director of environmental firm Beijing GeoEnviron (高能环境) from 2002 to 2009.
notes: Low media profile compared with chairman/founder Li Weiguo. Best route is the board secretary's office (stocks@yuhong.com.cn).

name: Han Xiao
current_role: Actual controller (~55.9%) of Shanghai Jundao Liquor Enterprise Development (formerly Rock/Shanghai Guijiu, ex-SSE: 600696, now delisted); no longer chairman
profile: Han Xiao (韩啸), in his mid-30s, became the actual controller and chairman of Shanghai-listed Rock Holdings, which was turned into a baijiu company (Shanghai Guijiu, later Jundao Liquor). He is the son of Han Hongwei of China Guijiu Group; the family's wealth was also tied to wealth manager HY Win Wealth. The listed company has since been delisted.
interesting_fact: The listed shell he controlled has one of the longest name histories on the Shanghai market: Fujian Haosheng -> Lijia -> Duolun -> Pitupi (匹凸匹) -> Rock (岩石) -> Jundao Liquor, before being delisted.
notes: CAUTION: Sept 2024 reports said Han Xiao was placed under criminal compulsory measures amid a police probe into an affiliate over suspected illegal fundraising (https://news.ycwb.com/2024-09/12/content_52923365.htm); company delisted. Not a suitable outreach target; no published contact.

name: Mo Haosong
profile: Mo Haosong (莫浩松) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2007-2013 with Mo Haotang, with wealth attributed to real-estate company 'Sangem'. No filings, company site or press coverage could be found to confirm the company's Chinese name, his role or current activities.
notes: Not identifiable from open sources: multiple Chinese and English searches for 莫浩松/莫浩棠 and 'Sangem' returned nothing relevant; company appears to be private. Last on Hurun in 2013. Would need the Chinese company name (or a Qichacha/registry lookup) to proceed.

name: Li Xiaoting
current_role: Vice Chairman and CEO (since June 2025), executive director, C-MER Medical Holdings (formerly C-MER Eye Care, HKEX: 3309)
profile: Li Xiaoting (李肖婷), 47, is co-controlling shareholder (with her husband, ophthalmologist Dr Dennis Lam Shun Chiu) of C-MER, a Hong Kong-listed eye-care and medical group operating clinics and hospitals in Hong Kong and mainland China. She ran its Hong Kong eye centre from 2012 and Shenzhen C-MER Hospital from 2013, and took over as vice chairman and CEO in June 2025.
interesting_fact: In a June 2025 board reshuffle, Dennis Lam stepped down and Li became vice chairman and CEO, while former Hong Kong health secretary Dr Ko Wing Man joined as independent non-executive director and vice chairman; C-MER returned to profit in FY2025 on revenue of about HK$1.95bn.
deep_cut_fact: She studied tourism management at Shenyang University (2001), took a postgraduate business diploma at Massey University in New Zealand (2004), and worked as project coordinator/executive officer at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2005-2009) before entering eye care.
notes: Company (not personal) social accounts; no published IR email found in the 2025 annual report. Company secretary is Chan Wa Ping (via registered office, Central, Hong Kong). She is a Pingshan (Shenzhen) CPPCC member.

name: Mark C Pigott
current_role: Executive Chairman, PACCAR Inc (Nasdaq: PCAR); Chairman of the DAF Trucks Supervisory Board
profile: Mark Pigott (born 1954) is the fourth generation of his family to lead PACCAR, the Bellevue, Washington maker of Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF trucks. He joined in 1978, was chairman and CEO from 1997 to 2014 (a period of ~1,700% total shareholder return), and has been executive chairman since 2014; he also presides over the PACCAR Foundation.
interesting_fact: A committed Anglophile and bibliophile, he sits on the boards of the British Library Foundation and Royal Shakespeare Company America and has led capital-project philanthropy at St Paul's Cathedral, London.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three Stanford degrees earned over 22 years - a BS in industrial engineering (1976), an MS in business (1984) and, while running PACCAR, a BA in humanities (1998) - and in 2014 founded the annual Pigott Poetry Prize in Ireland.
notes: Press contact is Ken Hastings, PACCAR Public Affairs (named on every earnings release). Pigott keeps a low personal media profile; arts/literary philanthropy (British Library, poetry prize, Trinity College Dublin) is a good conversational angle.

name: Kwok Chun Sing
current_role: Chairman and Executive Director, Envision Greenwise Holdings Ltd (晉景新能, HKEX: 1783)
profile: Kwok Chun Sing (郭晋昇), MH, JP, 52, has 25+ years in environmental technology and new energy. He vended his recycling business Chun Yang International into HK-listed Golden Ponder in 2022, became chairman in 2023 and renamed it Envision Greenwise; it now runs reverse-supply-chain and power-battery recycling, with FY to March 2026 revenue up 183% to HK$2.46bn.
interesting_fact: Envision Greenwise pitches itself at the junction of the energy transition and AI computing-driven metals demand: in FY2026 it commissioned its first battery-disposal line in the United States and upgraded its European HQ in Germany to build a global power-battery recycling network.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Hong Kong Recycling Chamber of Commerce in 2015 and still chairs it; he is also a director of CR Environmental Protection Technology Research (Shenzhen), a China Resources unit, and holds an EMBA from Macau University of Science and Technology.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (battery recycling, critical metals for AI/energy). Hurun lists him under China; he is Hong Kong-based (JP, Medal of Honour, Qingyuan CPPCC member).
